notes: *not able* is written as two words, so rule 35's cannot-fusion does not apply: the negative keeps only its *not* and the verb takes *thou art ... able*, headed on the complement under rule 44.

Each of the four כִּי particles takes the distinct English subordinator written for it — *if*, *so that*, *because*, *when* — and the bare infinitive שְׂאֵת holds its own *to* under rule 52's closing paragraph, no preposition standing before it.
